parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes cutting NHS waiting times through 40,000 more appointments per week and delivering the NHS long-term workforce plan, though these policies are framed around England's NHS and their impact on Scotland would depend on Barnett consequentials.

citations.quote: Cut NHS waiting times with 40,000 more appointments every week
We will deliver the NHS long-term workforce plan to train the staff we need to get patients seen on time.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservative manifesto does not directly address NHS waiting times in Scotland; its commitments on returning NHS performance to constitutional standards are framed around England's NHS.

citations.quote: We are committed to accelerating the NHS's recovery from the pandemic, delivering safe and effective services and ongoing improvements in waiting times for primary, elective, cancer and emergency care.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrat manifesto does not specifically address NHS waiting times in Scotland; its NHS policies are focused on England.

citations.quote: investing in public health and early access to community services, including GPs, pharmacists and dentists, so fewer people need to go to hospital in the first place

parties.name: SNP
parties.summary: The SNP commits to investing £300 million to drive down waiting times in Scotland's NHS, and calls on the UK Government to boost NHS spending by at least £10 billion extra per year, which would generate additional Barnett funding for Scotland.

citations.quote: we're determined to go further ­ including investing £300m to drive down waiting times ­ but we are doing that with one hand tied behind our back by Westminster.

Boost NHS spending by a minimum of £10bn extra each year to address rampant inflationary pressures and improve performance. This investment into NHS England would generate an additional £1bn annually for NHS Scotland to help meet increasing demand.
